name: Ibsam
overview: Ibsam is a male figure from the tribe of Issachar, identified in Scripture as the son of Tola. Beyond this paternal link, there are no additional details or notes recorded about him. His mention is concise, focusing primarily on his lineage within the tribal structure of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Ibsam means 'fragrance,' a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:2. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but its meaning may reflect a positive attribute or hope associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Ibsam is the son of Tola, establishing his place within the family line of the tribe of Issachar. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text regarding Ibsam.
scriptureSignificance: Ibsam's significance lies in his role as a descendant of Tola within the tribe of Issachar, contributing to the genealogical record that traces the heritage and tribal composition of Israel. His mention helps preserve the lineage and continuity of the tribe, which is important for understanding the broader biblical narrative of God's chosen people.
